title: Onramp Triage + Cadence Retrospective — 2028-11-20
body:
Onramp Triage + Cadence Retrospective — 2028-11-20

Attendees:
- Maya Chen (owner, SE lead)
- Diego Martinez (Field Eng)
- Sofia Patel (Customer Success)
- Riley Thompson (Solutions Eng)
- Jordan Lee (Delivery PM)
- Guest: Priya Rao (Customer eng for Tidewater) — joined for the Tidewater section

Meeting purpose / context:
Weekly cross-functional triage that combines the onramp cadence check (are onboarding customers moving through the runbook consistently?) with a short retro on recurring friction from the past two sprints. Goal: reduce block time for active onboarding customers, identify one process change to test next week.

Summary / quick hits:
- Net improvement: average blocker time down ~12% for customers in active onboarding compared to last week. Improvements driven by a new KMS troubleshooting checklist trial (PROSERV-4123).
- Biggest outstanding issue: intermittent KV-cache corruption seen in private deployments during long LLM sessions (INTEG-2897). Root cause unclear — reproducible on dedicated staging but not on hosted.
- Decided to run a 72-hour focused war-room for Tidewater (see action item A1) and trial a modified autoscale policy on one dedicated pool to capture metrics.

Agenda items covered:
1) Customer status roll (15 min)
2) Blocker deep-dive: KV-cache corruption (20 min)
3) Process improvement proposal: handoff checklist + async template (10 min)
4) Action items and owners (5 min)

Customer roll (current phase, nitty-gritty progress):
- Tidewater (large pilot, private deployment) — Phase: Load validation + regen testing.
  - Owner: Priya Rao (customer), Maya Chen (RSE).
  - Progress: Completed 3/4 validation scripts; observed KV cache mismatch when session tokens extended beyond 45 minutes.
  - Impact: Causes rare token mismatch and truncated generations in long-chat tests. Customer sees ~0.6% failure across long sessions.
  - Blockers: Debug logs insufficient at current verbosity; we need KV snapshotting at op-level. Linked: INTEG-2897.
  - Next steps: Start Tidewater war-room (A1), deploy debug build with fine-grained KV tracing to their staging pool (A2).

- MeridianHealth (mid-market, hosted with Dedicated reserve) — Phase: Canary rollout of quantized 4-bit model profile.
  - Owner: Riley Thompson.
  - Progress: Canary running on 2 nodes; latency looks good, small regressions in rare eval prompts (semantic drift).
  - Impact: Net cost down ~18% in canary; QA flagged 3 prompts with degraded output quality.
  - Blockers: Need to tune tokenization fallback; request Product to approve conservative rollback triggers for subscriber routes.
  - Next: Run a focused eval set and update rollback triggers (A3).

- Beacon Retail (SaaS client, hosted API) — Phase: Metrics and SLAs sign-off.
  - Owner: Diego Martinez.
  - Progress: Completed perf benchmarks and SLO doc sent. Awaiting legal sign-off on DPA changes for data retention.
  - Blockers: Legal review; no technical blockers.
  - Next: Chase counterparty legal and schedule sign-off call (A4).

Deep dive — KV-cache corruption (INTEG-2897):
- Observed behavior: Over long sessions (multi-turn > 45 min), generated outputs occasionally display truncated or misaligned system prompts. On staging dedicated pools, reproduction rate ~1/400 sessions. Not observed on hosted API.
- Hypothesis 1: KV cache eviction race when the background batcher reassigns slots across processes.
- Hypothesis 2: Pointer/offset drift from compilation-level kernel when model offload is triggered in dedicated environment.
- What we tried: Replayed failing sessions with elevated logging; toggled background batcher to single-threaded (reduces frequency but does not eliminate); swapped in non-quantized runtime (no change).
- Agreed debugging plan:
  - A2: Deploy KV snapshot tracing to Tidewater staging pool with time-bounded retention (owner: Maya) — collect 48 hours of failing traces.
  - A5: Add lightweight guard assertions in runtime to crash early if kv-index mismatch detected (owner: Riley) — dev PR planned for 2028-11-22.
  - A6: Provision one dedicated pool with `autoscale.min=2` and `autoscale.max=4` and background-batcher disabled (owner: Jordan) — to test whether orchestration is contributing.

Process retro / improvements:
- Pain point identified: handoffs from SE -> ProServices during high-volume weeks are missing a standardized set of artifacts (config snapshots, last-failed-jobs, expected SLOs). This forces re-requests and adds 8–10 hours of waste per customer on average.
- Quick experiment approved: create a one-page "handoff packet" template stored in Confluence and a Slack workflow (slash command) that attaches the packet to the customer channel.
  - A7: Riley to draft template by 2028-11-23.
  - A8: Diego to implement Slack slash command prototype by 2028-11-27.

Action items (owner — due — status):
- A1: Start Tidewater 72-hour war-room; invite infra and runtime SMEs — Maya Chen — DUE: 2028-11-21 — status: in_progress.
- A2: Deploy KV snapshot tracing build to Tidewater staging; capture first 48 hours — Maya Chen — DUE: 2028-11-23 — status: todo.
- A3: Run targeted evaluation suite for MeridianHealth canary and prepare rollback triggers for product sign-off — Riley Thompson + Product — DUE: 2028-11-24 — status: todo.
- A4: Schedule Beacon Retail legal sign-off call and send SLO appendix — Diego Martinez — DUE: 2028-11-22 — status: todo.
- A5: PR for runtime guard assertion to detect kv-index mismatch — Riley Thompson — DUE: 2028-11-22 — status: in_progress.
- A6: Provision dedicated pool variant with altered autoscale for repro testing — Jordan Lee — DUE: 2028-11-22 — status: todo.
- A7: Draft handoff packet template in Confluence — Riley Thompson — DUE: 2028-11-23 — status: todo.
- A8: Slash command prototype to auto-attach handoff packet to slack channels — Diego Martinez — DUE: 2028-11-27 — status: todo.

Risks / escalations:
- If KV corruption continues to leak into production for active customers, potential P1 for affected tenants. Current mitigations: limiting long-session timeouts (temporary), and increased monitoring.
- Legal bottleneck for Beacon may delay revenue recognition; Sofia to escalate to sales ops if no sign-off by 11/22.

Decisions made this meeting:
- Run Tidewater war-room with 72-hour window, include runtime, infra, and a dedicated on-call.
- Approved the handoff packet experiment (one-week trial), to be evaluated at next retro.

Notes to self / unresolved questions:
- Need to confirm whether dedicated pool compile-target flags differ from hosted defaults; Riley to get flag matrix from release-engineering.
- Determine whether KV snapshot tracing has privacy implications for private deployments (check with security).

Next meeting:
- Weekly triage same time next Tuesday (2028-11-27). If Tidewater war-room triggers, we will have daily 30-minute standups until resolution.

Appendix / quick refs:
- Repro session sample times (UTC): 2028-11-18 09:12, 2028-11-19 14:44 — traces attached in linked_artifacts (Confluence page).
- Primary contacts: Maya Chen (mchen@redwood.ai), Riley Thompson (rthompson@redwood.ai), Diego Martinez (dmartinez@redwood.ai).

End of notes.
